model.name: Current supplier onboarding
model.documentation: Current ordinary supplier onboarding from source evidence. Document transmission is not approval; Vendor Risk clearance is required before Master Data attempts record creation.

processes.name: Current supplier onboarding
processes.documentation: Covers ordinary supplier onboarding from form collection through screening and record-creation status. Unobserved appeal, urgent-bypass, and inconclusive-screening behavior remains outside the modeled path and is recorded as unresolved.

nodes.name: Create vendor record
nodes.documentation: Master Data attempts creation only after Vendor Risk clearance. The evidence does not equate clearance with successful record creation.

flows.name: Not completed
flows.condition: Vendor record creation did not complete

evidence.summary: Buyer collects tax and bank forms and sends the pack to Vendor Risk; Vendor Risk screens the supplier and sends a decision to Master Data.
The checklist names tax form, bank evidence, sanctions screening, and master-data creation.
Procurement no longer creates vendor records; Master Data creates them after Vendor Risk approval.

Vendor Risk clears, rejects, or requests missing evidence; clearance does not create the vendor record; Master Data creates it after clearance and reports whether creation completed. Appeal ownership, urgent screening bypass, and handling of inconclusive sanctions data were not observed.

decisions.description: Model Master Data as the current owner of vendor-record creation after Vendor Risk clearance, applying the dated correction and retaining prior Procurement ownership only as historical source context.
Treat sending documents as a handoff into screening, not as approval. The clearance branch from Vendor Risk is the gate to record creation.
Do not invent appeal ownership, an urgent screening bypass, or handling for inconclusive sanctions data; retain them as unresolved questions outside the ordinary modeled path.

issues.description: The dated correction records a change from prior Procurement ownership to current Master Data ownership for vendor-record creation.
Which team, if any, owns an appeal after Vendor Risk rejects onboarding?
Can an urgent exception bypass sanctions screening, and if so, who authorizes it?
How is the supplier handled when sanctions data is inconclusive?

links.assertion: Buyer collects the tax and bank forms.
Buyer sends the document pack to Vendor Risk without that transmission constituting approval.
Observed screening results are clearance, rejection, or a request for missing evidence.
Vendor Risk asks the Buyer for missing evidence.
Master Data creates the record only after clearance; the current owner supersedes prior Procurement ownership.
Clearance and record creation are distinct; Master Data reports whether creation completed.
Vendor Risk can reject onboarding; any appeal path remains unobserved.

scenarios.name: Supplier cleared and record created
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Master Data creates the vendor record after Vendor Risk clearance and tells the Buyer that creation completed.

scenarios.name: Missing evidence is supplied and rescreened
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The Buyer supplies requested evidence and Vendor Risk screens the supplier again before any approval or record creation.

scenarios.name: Onboarding rejected
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Onboarding ends as rejected; no appeal path is modeled because ownership is unobserved.

scenarios.name: Record creation does not complete
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Master Data tells the Buyer that record creation did not complete; the evidence does not describe further remediation.
